sourceEvidence.claim: Disabilities paragraphs 2-3 — direct address and assistance: under most circumstances talk directly to the patient; do not assume that nonverbal patients do not understand; accompanying caregivers can add information to any discussion as needed; ask if assistance is desired rather than assuming the patient cannot do something alone; most people, including people with disabilities, value their independence
sourceEvidence.quote:
Under most circumstances, talk directly to the patient. Do not assume that nonverbal patients do
not understand. Accompanying caregivers can add information to any discussion as needed.
Ask if assistance is desired rather than assuming the patient cannot do something alone. Most
people, including people with disabilities, value their independence.

sourceEvidence.claim: Disabilities paragraph 4 — speech difficulties: provide extra time for the interview; if speech is difficult to understand, consider asking them to write down a few words or ask them to rephrase their sentence; repeat what they said to ensure you understood it correctly
sourceEvidence.quote:
For patients with speech difficulties, provide extra time for the interview. If their speech is difficult

sourceEvidence.claim: Disabilities paragraph 5 — cognitive impairment: use concrete, specific language; ask simple, direct questions; eliminate background noise and distractions; do not assume the patient can read; adjust to how the patient understands best (eg, use hand gestures or ask them to demonstrate a task)
sourceEvidence.quote:
For patients with a cognitive impairment, use concrete, specific language. Ask simple, direct
questions. Eliminate background noise and distractions. Do not assume the patient can read.
Adjust to how the patient understands best (eg, use hand gestures or ask them to demonstrate a task).
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Disabilities paragraph 6 — deaf or hard of hearing: ask their preferred mode of communication; use light touch or waving to get their attention; for patients who prefer to speak and lipread, eliminate background noise, face the patient, and do not change your mode of speaking; consider using an interpreter when necessary
sourceEvidence.quote:
Ask patients who are deaf or hard of hearing their preferred mode of communication. Use light
touch or waving to get their attention. For patients who prefer to speak and lipread, eliminate
background noise, face the patient, and do not change your mode of speaking. Consider using an
interpreter when necessary.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Disabilities paragraph 7 — the two do-nots: do not bring up a disability if it is not relevant to a visit (eg, a patient in a wheelchair with an ear infection); do not skip relevant parts of the physical exam even if the disability makes the exam challenging

As with other parts of a medical history, do not bring up a disability if it is not relevant to a visit (eg,

even if the disability makes the exam challenging.

kypExtensions.summary: The 2+3+1 arc reading of the six printed techniques: TWO TO STRUCTURE the encounter (Introduction — name, pronouns, eye level, facing directly; Agenda setting — the joint agenda between the physician and the patient), THREE TO LISTEN (Reflection — synthesize what is offered, particularly the primary concern(s); Validation — legitimize or affirm perspectives; Recapitulation — summarize so far to ensure correct interpretation), ONE TO OPEN THE DOOR (Facilitation — free speech without guiding responses or leading questions, questions allowed throughout) — plus the claim that the printed order IS the working order of an encounter (the station-strip timeline).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the six techniques as parallel term/definition rows; the arc grouping, the station-strip timeline, and the structure/listen/open-the-door grammar are KYP's organization.
kypExtensions.location: core.why + core.keyIdea MOVE 1 + mechanisms[0] interview-arc-map + blocks[4] the steps block + the registry visual's Zone A station strip and 2+3+1 brackets

kypExtensions.summary: The emotion-response reading of PEARLS: an emotion surfacing mid-interview is the trigger the six interviewing techniques cannot answer, and PEARLS is the sequenced protocol that does — Partnership ('we' + preferred solutions), Empathy (name the emotion AND the why), Apology (own the physician's faults only), Respect (commend the printed list of constructive behaviors), Legitimization (normalize the response), Support (presence AND resources) — with the Empathy-vs-Legitimization and the half-response distractors (naming without the why; resources without presence) called out.
kypExtensions.rationale: PEARLS itself and all six definitions are the source's own (attributed, printed in red); the trigger→moves→rapport protocol framing, the pairing of moves, and the half-response distractor analysis are KYP's.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea MOVE 2 + mechanisms[1] pearls-rapport-map + blocks[2] the PEARLS table block caption + usmle.traps[0] + the registry visual's Zone B wheel

kypExtensions.summary: The ASK-DON'T-ASSUME synthesis of the disabilities block — the page's three ASKS (what terms they use; whether assistance is desired; the preferred mode of communication) against its three DO-NOT-ASSUMES (that nonverbal patients do not understand; that the patient cannot do something alone; that the patient can read) — plus the grouped-by-need panel (universal layer + the three need-specific protocols tagged TIME · SIMPLE · ATTENTION: speech gets extra time/write/rephrase/repeat; cognitive gets concrete simple language/quiet room/no assumed literacy/adjust the channel; deaf or hard of hearing gets attention first then the chosen channel).
kypExtensions.rationale: The seven paragraphs' rules are printed verbatim; the ask-vs-assume grammar, the need-based grouping, the TIME · SIMPLE · ATTENTION tags, and the paragraph labels (¶1–¶7) are KYP's.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea MOVE 3 + blocks[3] the verbatim list block + clinical[0] the adapted-interview block + blocks[5] the person-first/identity-first compare + the registry visual's Zone C panel

kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the printed page — 4 patterns (the Introduction choreography stem, the joint-agenda stem, the multiple-sclerosis PEARLS stem, the nonverbal-patient direct-address stem), 4 traps (Empathy vs Legitimization vs Validation; Reflection vs Recapitulation; Facilitation vs leading questions; talk-to-the-patient vs talk-to-the-caregiver), 3 pivots (the arc router, the emotion-router between blocks, the ask-don't-assume scanner), and 11 recall cards covering all six techniques, PEARLS, and the disabilities protocols.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid prints the definitions only; the attack structure, distractor designs, and question shapes are KYP's design.
